note: Edit this file to change what the review portal counts toward which standard. No lesson needs to change. 'standards' are local strands you can rename; 'codes' point them at an outside framework. Every code marked needsReview is my best match, not a verified alignment: check it against your district's documents before you report it to anyone. 'skills' maps a lesson's skill id to a strand. A key looks like course/lesson/skill, or course/skill when the skill id is already unique (chemistry and calculus ids start with chem. and calc.). A key ending in * matches any skill that starts with it.

PHYS-N1-A.title: Balanced forces and constant velocity
PHYS-N1-A.can: I can say what net force is, and use it to tell when an object keeps a constant velocity.

codes.title: Analyze data to support the claim that Newton's second law of motion describes the mathematical relationship among the net force on a macroscopic object, its mass, and its acceleration.
codes.note: Closest performance expectation. The first-law lesson builds toward it; it is not the same thing.

PHYS-N1-B.title: Inertia: objects keep their motion
PHYS-N1-B.can: I can use inertia to explain why objects keep moving, or stay still, when no net force acts.

codes.note: Closest performance expectation; confirm.

PHYS-N1-C.title: Reading and building force pictures
PHYS-N1-C.can: I can read motion pictures and force diagrams, and find the force that makes the net force zero.

codes.note: Closest performance expectation; confirm.

PHYS-N2-A.title: Net force and acceleration: a = F/m
PHYS-N2-A.can: I can use a = F/m to find acceleration, force or mass, and say how each change affects the others.

codes.title: Analyze data to support the claim that Newton's second law of motion describes the mathematical relationship among the net force on a macroscopic object, its mass, and its acceleration.
codes.note: Direct match for the second-law lesson; confirm against your district's documents.

PHYS-N2-B.title: Weight, falling and hanging masses
PHYS-N2-B.can: I can find weight from mass, and find the acceleration of falling or connected objects.

codes.title: Analyze data to support the claim that Newton's second law of motion describes the mathematical relationship among the net force on a macroscopic object, its mass, and its acceleration.
codes.note: Direct match for the second-law lesson; confirm against your district's documents.

PHYS-N2-C.title: Motion with a net force, friction included
PHYS-N2-C.can: I can find the net force when friction acts and link it to how an object moves.

codes.title: Analyze data to support the claim that Newton's second law of motion describes the mathematical relationship among the net force on a macroscopic object, its mass, and its acceleration.
codes.note: Direct match for the second-law lesson; confirm against your district's documents.

PHYS-F-A.title: Forces as interactions
PHYS-F-A.can: I can name the two objects in a force interaction and sort forces as contact or field forces.

codes.note: Closest performance expectation; confirm. Slot 4 target F1.

lesson.label: Free-Body Diagrams and Net Force lesson

PHYS-F-B.title: Free-body diagrams and net force
PHYS-F-B.can: I can draw a correct free-body diagram for an object in one dimension and find the net force from it.

codes.note: Closest performance expectation; confirm. Slot 4 target F3.

lesson.label: Free-Body Diagrams and Net Force lesson

PHYS-F-V.title: Vectors and ratios on a line
PHYS-F-V.can: I can add forces along a line, give the direction of a net force and reason with a ratio table.

codes.note: Prerequisite check for the forces unit; not an NGSS match.

lesson.label: Free-Body Diagrams and Net Force lesson

CHEM-ATOM-1.title: Atoms as an evidence-based model
CHEM-ATOM-1.can: I can tell what is argument and what is evidence, from Democritus to Dalton, and what a solid-ball atom cannot explain.

CHEM-ATOM-2.title: Conservation of mass and definite proportions
CHEM-ATOM-2.can: I can use fixed mass ratios (like 8 g O per 1 g H in water) and show that mass is conserved in a reaction.

codes.title: Use mathematical representations to support the claim that atoms, and therefore mass, are conserved during a chemical reaction.
codes.note: Good match for conservation of mass. Definite proportions is part of the same reasoning.

CHEM-ATOM-3.title: Multiple proportions and atom mass ratios
CHEM-ATOM-3.can: I can compare the recipes of compounds made from the same elements and use whole-number ratios to reason about atoms.

codes.note: Related; multiple proportions goes beyond the performance expectation. Confirm.

CHEM-ATOM-4.title: The nuclear atom from evidence
CHEM-ATOM-4.can: I can use scattering data to explain why the plum-pudding model failed and what the results show about the nucleus.

CHEM-ATOM-5.title: Counting particles in atoms, ions and isotopes
CHEM-ATOM-5.can: I can find the protons, neutrons and electrons of any atom, ion or isotope from its symbol, and write the symbol from the counts.

codes.note: Foundation skill. HS-PS1-1 uses electron patterns to predict properties; this lesson builds the particle counts it rests on. Confirm.
Foundation skill for predicting reaction outcomes from electrons. Confirm.

CHEM-ATOM-6.title: Coulomb's law as a proportion
CHEM-ATOM-6.can: I can use Coulomb's law as a proportion (double the distance, quarter the force; double a charge, double the force) to predict how strongly an electron is held.

codes.note: Supports the electron-pattern reasoning HS-PS1-1 rests on. Confirm.
Foundation for predicting outcomes from how strongly electrons are held. Confirm.

CHEM-LAB-1.title: Working safely in the lab
CHEM-LAB-1.can: I put on protective equipment before handling chemicals and avoid hazards.

CHEM-LAB-2.title: Carrying out an investigation and using the data
CHEM-LAB-2.can: I follow a procedure, record data, and use it to identify an unknown.

CALC-DER-1.title: Derivative rules you already know
CALC-DER-1.can: I can differentiate powers, sums, and the basic functions (e^x, ln x, sin x, cos x).

codes.note: Differentiation unit. I have not matched a more specific learning objective: add the code your course uses.

CALC-DER-2.title: The product rule
CALC-DER-2.can: I can differentiate a product of functions with f'g + fg' and explain why (fg)' is not f'g'.

codes.note: Product and quotient rules in the AP course framework, as best I recall. Verify the code against your copy of the Course and Exam Description.
